headline_result: THE FUSED OUTPUT PASSES ITS DISCRIMINATION GATE AND LOSES FIRM SEPARATION. These are two different properties and both are measured here. The fused matrix is not degenerate -- 323,424 distinct affinity values over 8,596,731 pairs. But on the locked sec-6.3 cohort, scale-free rank AUC falls from 0.7429 (view 1 alone) to 0.5114 fused, against 0.5 = no separation, while view 2 alone is 0.5203. THE FUSION TRACKS THE WEAKER VIEW. This is a real and reportable result, not a defect in the run: PRD sec 6.3 asks whether firm separation SURVIVES fusion, and on this experiment, at this carrier, it does not.

value.what_a_reader_must_change_to_falsify: Re-run with a different (K, T). If the fused ranking moves materially, the result is an artefact of the parameter pair and not of the data. I RAN THAT: K=30 T=10 against K=20 T=20 gives Spearman rho 0.9848 and top-decile Jaccard 0.9157 over 8,596,731 pairs -- the output is stable under a materially different setting, so it is not a one-choice artefact. The stronger falsifier is the firm result itself: if AUC had RISEN under the alternative, my headline claim would be parameter-dependent. It does not.

evidence.positive_control: the two settings agree at rho 0.9848 / J 0.9157 -- high enough that the fusion is not chasing the parameters, and NOT 1.0, so the comparison is a real one rather than the same computation twice
evidence.failure_look: a parameter chosen to make the answer come out -- the weighted-sum objection wearing SNF's name. The defence is that both parameters are the method's published defaults, fixed before the outcome was seen, and the alternative run is reported whatever it showed

value.evaluator: FUSED(i,j) is element (i,j) of SNF([W1, W2], K=20, T=20) over the 4,147 co-measured entities in ascending population-index order, symmetrised as (F + F^T)/2. W1(i,j) = (runs placing i,j in one block)/25; W2(i,j) = |Fam(i) & Fam(j)| / |Fam(i) | Fam(j)|.
value.consumer_contract: Resolve the two pinned inputs, rebuild W1 and W2 by the evaluator above, run SNF at the declared parameters, take the upper triangle in ascending index order as float32, and verify sha256 == fused_values_sha256. Reconstruction rather than transport, because 8,596,731 float32 values is ~34 MB and the inputs are already pinned.

coverage_masks.why_the_fused_domain_is_not_the_union: SNF requires BOTH views to carry evidence for a pair. View 1 is MEASURED on all 19,482; view 2 on 4,147 (15,335 ABSENT, 78.7%). The fused affinity therefore exists on the CO-MEASURED 4,147. The remaining 15,335 are carried ABSENT for the FUSED feature and MEASURED for view 1 -- they are not dropped and they are not zero. THE UNION IS THE RECORD; the co-measured set is where a fused VALUE can exist. Additionally 68 view-2 members fall outside the population entirely and are excluded by the population's own definition.

scale_free_AUC.definition: P(a within-firm pair outranks a cross-firm pair); 0.5 = no separation. Rank-based, so it is invariant under ANY monotone rescaling.
scale_free_AUC.why_AUC_and_not_the_mean_difference: MY FIRST INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG AND I AM RECORDING IT. I computed within- minus cross-firm MEAN affinity and read a collapse from 0.1713 (view 1) to 0.0000175 (fused). That comparison is invalid: SNF row-normalises to a transition matrix, so the fused maximum is 0.004846 while view 1's is 1.0, and a raw-mean difference across them measures the NORMALISATION as much as the separation. The rank AUC is invariant to that and is the instrument this row uses. The finding survives the correction -- 0.7429 -> 0.5114 -- but it would have been reported for the wrong reason, and a reader could have refuted the number while the conclusion stood.

raw_means_retained_for_audit.caveat: NOT comparable across views; retained only so a reader can re-derive.

prd_6_3_input_not_discharge.observation: On this experiment firm separation does NOT survive fusion: AUC falls from 0.7429 on view 1 alone to 0.5114 fused, against 0.5 = no separation, while view 2 alone carries 0.5203. THE FUSION TRACKS THE WEAKER VIEW. The mechanism is visible in the inputs rather than mysterious: view 2 is near-uniform with respect to firms, and SNF's cross-diffusion lets a near-uniform view flatten a discriminating one.
prd_6_3_input_not_discharge.what_this_is_not: This does NOT discharge sec 6.3 and does NOT declare it failed. Wave 2 SUPPLIES the baselines; the test runs when the design lane runs it. The PRD's 0.989 / 0.974 were measured on DIFFERENT views over a DIFFERENT population and are not the bar. And the result is scoped exactly as ruled: on the 1,820 cohort entities inside the fused domain, firm label INFERRED by parse, with 17,541 of the population outside 6.3's denominator entirely.

what_this_wave_may_not_claim: 6.1 (rename), 6.2 (persistence) and 6.5 (portability) are L4 and are NOT claimed here; a completion claim naming any of them as PASSED would be false. 6.4 is discharged with its shape changed -- three gate runs: view 1 re-stated over this population, view 2 earning its own, and this fused output re-gated as the third. 6.3 is SUPPLIED.
